topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: Key-Value Memory
lecture_lines: MLPs act as the model's long-term memory vault.
Attention selects; MLPs store actual facts.
Picture a library bookshelf inside the transformer.
animations: Create a box labeled 'Memory Vault' (#FFFFFF) to represent the MLP.
Animate 'Attention' icons (#00FFFF) hovering above the vault.
Show a 'Bookshelf' inside the vault with 'Fact' entries (#FFD700).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Neuron as a Pattern Matcher
lecture_lines: Neurons function as pattern-matching light dimmers.
Input matches weight pattern; neuron fires.
Higher layers recognize more abstract concepts.
animations: Flash input signals (#FFA500) arriving at the neuron.
Display 'Pattern Matched' text (#00FFFF) near the output.

sections.title: Mechanism: Key-Value Memory Pairs
lecture_lines: MLPs function as Key-Value memory systems.
Expansion layer acts as the detecting Key.
Projection layer inserts the factual Value.
animations: Animate an input 'Query' (#FFFFFF) interacting with the 'Key' matrix.
Reveal the resulting 'Value' vector (#00FF00) retrieved from the pair.

sections.title: Visualizing Weight Updates
lecture_lines: Training rotates weights toward new data points.
Imagine a vector aligning with a Fact.
Weights minimize the distance to true facts.
animations: Show an initial weight vector (#FFFFFF) as an arrow.
Animate the vector rotation (#FF0000) towards a 'Fact' target.
Display the 'Final Weight' alignment (#00FF00) to the target.

sections.title: Conclusion: Distributed Representation
lecture_lines: Facts exist across the distributed network.
No single cell holds one specific fact.
Holographic storage requires retraining to change.
animations: Show a wide-angle grid of neurons (#FFFFFF) interconnected.
Animate a signal propagating through multiple neurons (#FF00FF).
Fade the background to show the 'Distributed Pattern' (#00FFFF).
